TO BE UPDATED BY LAOS TEAM
The key indicative activities are: Pillar 1. GEDSI and Feminist Influencing: 1) Oxfam country team Mainstreaming GEDSI Base into project operational guidelines to promote community action, more inclusive water governance, resilience and climate actions, and community action on climate resilience. 2) Feminist community research also known as Sao Baan/villagers, Community Action Research, and Feminist Participatory Action Research supported/facilitated by academic and CSO partners (research topicis water management, water security, climate impact, GESID impact from disaster risk and climate resilience) o Adapt the existing tool of research from IP2 and ensure that the GEDSI will be included. 3) Support for increased use of GEDSI analysis including GenderGEDSI Impact Assessment (includes care climate nexus) among partners, community, and targeted stakeholders. 4) Linking-learning, and networking between community researchers nationally and regionally-Year 2-Year 4. Thisincludes the regional networking and exchange between women leaders (including women leaders of CSOs network in the country) and leaders from marginalised social groups including the Women and Rivers Congress and also participation in events held by others. This will be included support for participation, representation and leadership of women and marginalised social groups (disability, indigenous people etc) in dialogue events at all levels. This includes network building and strengthening, tailored learning events, preparatory meetings, and convening of dialogue events or support to participate in events convened by other stakeholders. 5) Support Feminist Community Driven Initiatives to facilitate community participatory planning and decision-making
Pillar 2. Water Resource Governance (WRG): 1) Grants to diverse CSOs and networks at sub-national, national and regional levels. This includes Partner Capacity Assessments, co-planning, and program (includes GEDSI mainstreaming) awareness raising andcapacity building. 2) Laos- Support CSO participation through LCCC and authority through MoNRE and MoLSW, MRC in WRG dialogue events at sub-national, national and regional levels. This includes learning events, preparatory meetings, and convening of dialogue events or support to participate in events convened by other stakeholders. Key WRG issues include planned water development projects, and related laws and policies and their implementation, GEDSI, social and environment impact assessment and policyon mainstream and tributary dams in Cambodia, Laos, Thailand and Manganma; review of the Power Purchase Agreement for the Pak Beng Dam, people’s impact assessment of the Yuom-Saleen Diversion project, and laws and policies on outward investments in waterinfrastructure in Thailand; national dialogue event (multiple macro thematic issues) in Lao PDR; and impact of climate change in the Mekong Delta (Vietnam). 3) Youth film competition on water security and inclusive sustainable investment, includes Establishing a feminist youth river network in the nation 4) Facilitate the National Dialogue on water governance, water security, and inclusive sustainable investment
Pillar 3. Climate Resilience: 1) Facilitate the National and Regional Water Security and Climate Resilience dialogue as a platform for water and climate policy influence (variety of research and case studies and publications...) 2) Facilitate community organisation and capacity strengthening related to disaster risk management including areview of current structures in riverine communities. Voice of women, people living with disability <(>&<)> other marginalised groups in climate policy, economy resilience, and practice and facilitate community vulnerability mapping and disaster/climate risk management activities. with relevant local authorities including sub national disaster risk management structures. 3) Support Voice of women, people living with disability <(>&<)> other marginalised groups in climate policy, economy resilience, and practice andfacilitate community vulnerability mapping through planning and decision making, investment and implementation preprocess 4) Support grant for community livelihood development, sustainable production, and women's economic empowerment linking with bothnature-based and technology-based solutions documentation and dissemination of climate resilient livelihood demonstrations (this could be conducted after completion and present the community’s research result). Livelihood activity and economic resilient (sustainable production and consumption), grand provided after research results and community planning to invest for example:  Nature-based solution for climate resilience  Agroecological activities for community level  Diversification of Climate Smart Agriculture Practices  Green business and circling production  Fish species extension/conservation zone
5) Laos- Support economic resilience and just energy transition competition towards realizing climate and economic resilience of communitiesin the Mekong River through the Ecothon (Eco-entrepreneurs’ Marathon), this is a sustainable and innovative business model competition that provides a selected group of startups in the ASEAN region to promote the use of services and related products, which respond to basic needs and bring a better quality of life while minimizing the use of natural resources and toxic materials as well as the emissions of waste and pollutants over the life cycle of the service or product so as not to jeopardize the needs of future generations across the ASEAN region

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam has had a presence in Lao PDR for longer than most INGOs, with both Oxfam in Belgium (OBE) and Oxfam Australia (OAU) beginning programming and establishing offices in the late 1980s. Oxfam’s vision is of a Laos in which all citizens – particularlywomen, the marginalised and discriminated groups – are able to claim their right to access opportunities and resources so as to overcome all forms of poverty and injustice.
Since 2015, the work of Oxfam in the country is governed by the Oxfam Country Strategy (2015-2019).We seek transformative changes in policies, practices and beliefs in ways that fundamentally improve the lives of poor and marginalised women and men, and ensure that all citizens have the same opportunities to enjoy their rights. Todo so, Oxfam focuses its work on four Domains of Change: Citizen Participation and Civil Society Development, Gender Justice, Resilient Communities and Sustainable Development, and Responsible Investment.
For this project, Oxfam in Laos will support theexpansion of the influencing work and public campaign on advocating for more inclusive social protection and access to social protection of the most marginalized workers. National public events will be organised, such Eliminate Violence Against Women Day(EVAW), and digital platforms will be used to socialize the information, and stir discussion and dialogue among rights holders, government stakeholders and policy makers. The campaigns will be implemented nationwide and in the provinces where Oxfam in Laos works. Target groups include marginalized workers, youth,women, CSOs as well as government stakeholders.
